The Government Secondary School, Masharkut, in Butura District of Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State, has been burnt down following a fire outbreak on Sunday afternoon. The Chairman of Bokkos Local Government Area, Amalau Samuel Amalau, confirmed the incident to PUNCH Online in Jos, the state capital, when contacted on Sunday. “It’s true that the school building was set ablaze. It happened today,” the chairman said. Asked whether it was terrorists who set the building ablaze, Amalau said the cause of the fire and those responsible could not yet be ascertained. “How will I know? We only saw the school on fire. We cannot ascertain for now what it is and who is responsible. It happened today,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The incident reportedly caused panic among residents of the community after smoke was sighted rising from the school premises shortly after church service. Some members of the community have, however, blamed the fire incident on bandits who they said have been operating in the area. A resident, Daniel Bwehfa, said residents initially noticed smoke coming from the school before discovering, about 30 minutes later, that the building was on fire. Bwehfa alleged that some suspected bandits had been using the school premises as a sleeping place, claiming that people were often seen gathering within the compound in the evenings. He, however, did not provide further details about the identities of those allegedly seen around the school or establish whether they were responsible for the fire. “Some strangers whom we suspect to be bandits have been coming to that school. We don’t know their mission. This has been a source of concern to community members. If they are not the people who set the school on fire, who else might have done that ?” Bwelfa wondered. The latest incident has heightened concerns over the safety of public institutions and educational facilities in communities affected by insecurity in parts of Bokkos LGA. Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation, including the Spokesperson for the Plateau State Police Command, Alabo Alfred, were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. James Abraham
